first.rationale: Activation and onboarding are both declining, and the two most directly relevant archived findings indicate that reducing signup friction and shortening onboarding improved activation, completion, and time-to-value. I would verify both records before committing. The experiment should focus on onboarding rather than promotional pricing, which previously hurt 30-day retention. Sustainable qualified-revenue impact remains uncertain, so the test should monitor downstream qualification and retention, not only completion and activation.

final.rationale: Run a guarded onboarding-simplification experiment for SMB and simple-workspace accounts only. The verified evidence supports improved activation, completion, and qualified revenue in SMB/simple accounts, while showing a material 60-day churn increase for complex workspaces when setup steps are removed. Exclude complex-workspace accounts, and measure activation, completion, time-to-value, qualified revenue, and retention. This addresses both current activation and onboarding declines without using promotional pricing that previously harmed retention.
